body:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Page: high p95 latency observed for inference-api in us-west. Alerts from perf-monitor: p50 ≈ 120ms -> 300ms, p95 ≈ 480ms -> 2300ms. Pager: @Ops Oncall you're up.
Ops Oncall: I'm on it, looking at dashboard now.
Alex H.: seeing a sharp jump at 03:12 UTC across many pods. CPU steal & syscall counts spike on a subset of nodes.
Maya R.: I can share a quick histogram and top traces. Link: https://logs.internal/r/abc123 (log bundle)
Jordan L.: hypothesis: kernel patch that landed to node-image-v18 last night may have changed scheduler or preempt settings; we saw similar in canary earlier but not triaged.
Liam S.: confirm nodes with spikes are using image-v18c. Others on v17 are fine.
Kim P.: requesting sample trace ids for slow requests so we can correlate spans and kernel transitions.
Alex H.: sample traces: trace: trc-44a, trc-47b, trc-5f2. Shared spans show long syscall durations in accept()/read() and a few context-switch bursts.
Maya R.: here's an extracted span snippet:
```
span_id: s-5f2
service: inference-api
duration_ms: 1820
span_events: [kernel-syscall:1200ms, user-processing:600ms]
```
Jordan L.: perf counters from node n-09: context-switches up 8x, syscalls/sec up 6x, softirqs also elevated. Attaching perf stat output: https://perf.internal/attach/987
Ops Oncall: mitigation suggestion: cordon affected nodes and shift traffic, try rolling back to v17 on a test pod.
Liam S.: doing cordon of n-07,n-09 now; draining one to validate. `kubectl cordon n-09 && kubectl drain n-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Eng-trace-bot: tracked traces for thread: trc-44a,trc-47b,trc-5f2
Kim P.: while draining, please collect `perf record -a -g --sleep 10` and `dmesg | tail -n 200` from one affected host.
Alex H.: dmesg shows repeated preempt events and syscall latency warnings around 03:11:37.
Maya R.: timeline so far: 02:58 normal, 03:10 small uptick, 03:12 spike correlates with rolling update of node-image-v18 to 30% of fleet, 03:16 automated autoscale kicked, 03:18 p95 still high.
Jordan L.: hypothesis A: kernel scheduler or uintptr alignment change in v18 causing syscall path to monopolize CPU in certain workloads. Hypothesis B: new kernel preemption config interacts badly with our affinity settings.
Kim P.: can someone grep for the specific kernel commit id on n-09? `uname -a` + `/boot/config-*` would help.
Liam S.: grabbed uname: `Linux n-09 6.3.11-custom-v18c` commit: 9f4a2b3; sending to eng-security channel for build artifact lookup.
Ops Oncall: customer impact: ~3% error budget burn, some requests slow but not failing. Notifying customer success for potential escalations.
Maya R.: short-term mitigations: 1) shift traffic off v18 nodes; 2) revert node image to v17 in canary pool; 3) keep p99 watch. Doing 1 now.
Alex H.: after cordon and traffic shift p95 dropped from 2300ms -> 520ms for traffic on v17 nodes. We're seeing recovery on the non-v18 pool.
Jordan L.: action items: (A) collect perf traces and kernel configs from affected nodes (assigned: Liam), (B) repro with a microbenchmark stressing syscalls (assigned: Alex), (C) produce RCA doc with timelines/log bundles (assigned: Maya).
Liam S.: attaching perf record link: https://perf.internal/rec/abc987 and dmesg snapshot link: https://logs.internal/dmesg/n-09
Kim P.: recommend escalating to platform release to halt further v18 rollouts and add a gating check for syscall-rate regression in canary.
Ops Oncall: added incident tag and updated status page: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incident/1758123456
Maya R.: compiling the in-incident RCA notes and will start a doc -> link: https://docs.internal/incident-1758123456
Alex H.: thanks everyone, will follow up with repro steps and perf artifacts. :white_check_mark:
